body:
Oof, I did a little bit of research, and it turns out this is actually allowed behaviour in the GLSL specification:

> Note that implementations may use a cheap approximation to the remainder, and the error can be large due to the discontinuity in floor. This can produce mathematically unexpected results in some cases, such as mod(x,x) computing x rather than 0, and can also cause the result to have a different sign than the infinitely precise result.

Source: https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/GLSLangSpec.4.60.html#common-functions

> AMD drivers on Windows are really bad for Vulkan/OpenGL Can confirm that switching `rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows` project setting to `d3d12` makes the issue go away indeed. > Oof, I did a little bit of research, and it turns out this is actually allowed behaviour in the GLSL specification: Yikes. Actually seems like `x / x` on its own is problematic here as it's slightly less than `1.0`. And in such case both `floor(x / x) == 0.0` and `mod(x, x) == x - x * floor(x / x) == x` kinda make sense. | -|- `x / x != 1.0` being allowed by the specification seems very strange to me. But assuming that's indeed the case (and thus we can't expect this to be fixed within the drivers) I think it would be good to modify our particle animation frame calculation (which I've mentioned is broken because of this issue) to work around it. #110437 works for me.
